subject: general
question: The distance of the foot of a 20 m high tower from a point on the ground is 20√3 m. What is the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from this point?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Height of **tower** (P) = 20 m

Distance from **foot** (B) = 20√3 m

Ratio P : B = 20 : 20√3 = 1 : √3

In a **right-angled triangle**, if the ratio of side opposite to θ and adjacent side is 1 : √3, then θ = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the **tower** (AB) = 20 m

Distance of point C from **foot** B (BC) = 20√3 m

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe6e6a8026f7ad725108ddd95676aed2b9a3779b42bd8788ff7dcadfb48c511e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔABC, tan θ = AB / BC

⇒ tan θ = 20 / (20√3)

⇒ tan θ = 1 / √3

⇒ Since tan 30° = 1 / √3

⇒ θ = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

For specific angles: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Angle of Elevation

The **angle of elevation** is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object.

30-60-90 Triangle Property

In a 30-60-90 triangle, the sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2, where 1 is opposite to 30° and √3 is opposite to 60°.</p
